title: Affinity handshake slip produced unintended model substitutions; rollback runbook & preventative controls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: During a routine routing-policy rollout, a timing gap in the affinity handshake logic allowed stale affinity tokens to bind to incompatible model flavors. This caused a subset of routed requests to be served by incorrect, lower-capacity model variants, amplifying latency and error rates for affected customers. We rolled back the policy release and implemented short-term mitigations; this ticket tracks action items and runbook changes to prevent recurrence.
incident_description: At 2026-02-18T10:12:00Z a config change to routing policy precedence was pushed to production. The new precedence interacts with sticky-affinity reconciliation in the policy broker. A race between policy propagation and the affinity-service reconciliation loop led to affinity tokens being re-associated to older model flavor tags that were not compatible with the request shape. The mismatch triggered silent fallback paths and increased slow tails and 5xxs for affected routes. Roughly 4% of global requests during the window experienced elevated latency and a 0.9% error spike; several paying customers reported intermittent failures.
timeline: 2026-02-18T10:12:00Z - New routing precedence policy released (canary to 5%).
2026-02-18T10:18:00Z - First alert: route-level P50/P95 latency deviation detected by Console alerting.
2026-02-18T10:29:00Z - Observed mismatch pattern: affinity tokens had flavor tags older than policy snapshot; increased fallback to quantized variants noted.
2026-02-18T10:35:00Z - Manual rollback of routing precedence policy to previous snapshot initiated.
2026-02-18T10:42:00Z - Rollback complete; immediate drop in tail latency and fallback rate confirmed.
2026-02-18T11:05:00Z - Incident declared resolved; post-incident analysis kicked off.
2026-02-20T09:00:00Z - Root cause analysis draft completed and reviewed with runtime and routing ownership.
2026-02-24T15:30:00Z - Short-term mitigations onboarded to staging for validation (affinity TTL harmonization, safety gate in policy broker).
detection: Console route-level latency anomaly alert keyed to route: /v1/generate-chat
Customer support tickets reporting transient 5xx for high-throughput customers
Increased fallback telemetry in the model-selection ledger (fallback_rate metric up 12x on canary shards)
mitigation: Immediate rollback of the routing precedence change to the previous stable snapshot (2026-02-18T10:35:00Z)
Disabled sticky-affinity reconciliation for the canary cohort while we validated token/variant compatibility
Scaled up dedicated capacity and enabled explicit variant pinning for impacted customers to keep service functional during investigation
postmortem_findings: Affinity handshake is implemented as a two-step reconciliation: policy snapshot propagation and token retagging. The two steps assume near-synchronous propagation but lacked guards for transient desync.

Affinity tokens carried 'flavor_tag' values without version-pinning; when policy precedence changed, older flavor_tags were still considered valid by the fast-path selection code, causing silent substitution.
Policy broker lacked a safety gate that verifies token flavor compatibility before assigning to local routing cache.
Telemetry lacked fine-grained correlation between token_id -> flavor_tag evolution and per-request selection traces, making root cause identification slower than ideal.
Unit/integration tests covered static policy state but not the dynamic propagation race under realistic SSE propagation latencies.
action_items: RB-01: Add safety gate in policy broker to verify flavor compatibility before committing token retagging. Owner: Marcus Lee. Due: 2026-03-02.
RB-02: Harmonize affinity token TTLs and policy snapshot TTLs to prevent short-lived snapshot mismatches. Owner: Nadia Chen. Due: 2026-03-05.
RB-03: Implement a short-circuit that rejects token retagging if policy snapshot age > 3s for canary cohorts. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2026-03-01.
RB-04: Create an automated rollback check that simulates token/variant compatibility post-policy-rollout before enabling canary traffic. Owner: Runtime-test team (Evan Ortiz). Due: 2026-03-10.
RB-05: Add a synthetic test that exercises policy+affinity propagation under variable propagation latencies (0-30s) as part of CI. Owner: SRE Test Infra (Liam Park). Due: 2026-03-12.
RB-06: Expand telemetry to join token_id, flavor_tag, policy_snapshot_id and request_id for causal tracing. Owner: Telemetry team (Maya Ortiz). Due: 2026-02-28.
RB-07: Update incident runbook with explicit steps for affinity-related rollbacks and a checklist to verify variant compatibility. Owner: On-call lead (Riley Novak). Due: 2026-02-26.
RB-08: Customer-facing postmortem and targeted outreach to top affected accounts. Owner: Customer Success (Jordan Price). Due: 2026-02-25.
runbook_changes: Add a new section 'Affinity Handshake Failures' with decision trees for rollback vs. mitigation
Include 'policy_snapshot_age' checks in pre-rollout gating steps
Document the commandsets and dashboards used to trace token_id -> flavor_tag mappings across regions
Define post-rollback validation steps: monitor fallback_rate, P99 latency, and a synthetic request set for 30 minutes
telemetry_changes: Emit flavor_tag transitions as explicit events in the model-selection ledger
Create a new dashboard that surfaces token_id churn and flavor_tag mismatch ratio by region
Add an alert rule: flavor_tag_mismatch_ratio > 0.5% for 5m for any production shard triggers pager
tests_and_validation: Integration test that replays policy snapshot sequences with injected propagation delays and asserts no token retagging to incompatible flavors
Load test that ensures policy broker safety gate does not add >1ms median overhead to selection path under p95 load
Canary gating job that runs compatibility checks for 10k synthetic tokens before enabling traffic to new policy snapshot
rollout_plan: Implement and validate safety gate in staging with synthetic token sweep
Deploy to a small canary cohort (1% traffic) with strict snapshot-age checks and enhanced telemetry
If canary stable for 48h with no flavor_tag_mismatch alerts, gradually expand to 10% then 50% and full rollout
Maintain fast rollback capability and run automated compatibility checks during each step
communication: Customer outreach: template prepared for affected accounts; CS leads notified
Status page: brief incident note posted at 2026-02-18T12:00:00Z and updated when resolved
Postmortem doc link shared with Execs and GTM two days after incident
risks_and_open_questions: Does the current token model scale if we add more compatibility checks in the hot-path? Need performance validation.
Edge cases: cross-region propagation latencies may exceed harmonized TTL during major cloud events — how to adjust adaptive TTLs?
Long-term: should we transition affinity tokens to include explicit model-version hashes to avoid flavor ambiguity?
notes: This incident surfaced a class of race-condition bugs in stateful routing systems where eventual consistency assumptions leak into fast-path selection.
Prior related tickets addressed variant misrouting but focused on fallback loops; this ticket focuses on token/handshake correctness and pre-rollout validation.
Recommend a small cross-functional working group (runtime + routing + telemetry + SRE) for the next two sprints to close out RB items.
